BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p81/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p81/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p81/r5.claim: The Qur’an characterizes its opponents as contentious and obstinate, framing their polemics as argument rather than a genuine demonstration of ability.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p81/r5.anchor: وقد وصفهم الله تعالى في كتابه بالجدل واللدد

NAHHAS:v3p29/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p29/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p29/r6.claim: Ludd is the plural of aladd, like ṣumm is the plural of aṣamm.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r8.claim: God made this unmatched Qur'an easy in clear, eloquent Arabic so the Prophet can give glad tidings to the God-fearing and warn the stubborn disputants.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r9.claim: The God-fearing guard against what angers God, neither suppressing truth nor legitimizing falsehood, and promptly repent when they slip.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r9.anchor: يجعلون بينهم وبين ما يسخط الله وقاية , فلا يبطلون حقا

BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r10.claim: Lidd describes someone who persists in error and hostility, refuses evidence, and tries to turn truth into falsehood out of contempt and arrogance.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r10.anchor: هو الذي يتمادى في غيه ولا يرجع لدليل , ويركب

BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r11.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports the Prophet defining pride as rejecting truth and despising people, distinguishing it from simply liking fine clothes and shoes; cited from Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r11.anchor: ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال :

BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r12.claim: Persistent arrogance makes a person liable to die in disbelief, the gravest falsehood, and be barred from Paradise.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r12.anchor: فكان جديرا بأن يركبه الله أبطل الباطل : الكفر

DURR-FULL:v5p545/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p545/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p545/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses ludd as wicked or sinful people.
DURR-FULL:v5p545/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وتنذر به قوما لدا} قال: فجارا

DURR-FULL:v5p545/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p545/r7.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p545/r7.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله: {لدا} قال: صما

DURR-FULL:v5p545/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p545/r8.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v5p545/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses ludd as adversarial disputants.
DURR-FULL:v5p545/r8.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله: {لدا} قال: خصماء

DURR-FULL:v5p545/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p545/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p545/r9.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {قوما لدا} قال: جدلا بالباطل

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r8.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r8.claim: It means persistent disputants; the image comes from medicine placed at the sides of the mouth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r8.anchor: الثاني : أهل إلحاح في الخصومة , مأخوذ

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r9.speaker: الشاعر
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r9.claim: A cited poem uses liddad of hostile, persistent dispute.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r9.anchor: بغوا لددي حنقا علي كأنما … تغلي عداوة صدرهم في مرجل

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r10.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r10.claim: It means people arguing falsely, from liddud, a severe disputant.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r10.anchor: مأخوذ من اللدود وهو شديد الخصومة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r11.speaker: الشاعر
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r11.claim: A second poem describes disputing with people marked by intense argument.

MUQATIL:19:96-98/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:96-98/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:96-98/r2.claim: God made the Quran clear on Muhammad's tongue to bring glad tidings to monotheists and warn people with its threats.
MUQATIL:19:96-98/r2.anchor: { فإنما يسرناه بلسانك } ، يقول: فإنما بيناه على لسانك يا محمد، يعني القرآن،

MUQATIL:19:96-98/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:96-98/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:96-98/r3.claim: Ludd means disputants who argue obstinately in falsehood, as in 2:204, which he connects to al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq.
MUQATIL:19:96-98/r3.anchor: قوما لدا } [آية: 97]، يعني جدلاء خصماء بالباطل، نظيرها في البقرة:

THALABI:v6p233/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p233/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p233/r5.claim: God made the Qur'an easy in Muhammad's tongue to give glad tidings to the pious and warn disputatious people.
THALABI:v6p233/r5.anchor: فإنما يسرناه سهلناه يعني القرآن بلسانك يا محمد لتبشر به المتقين

THALABI:v6p233/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p233/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p233/r6.claim: He glosses لدا as fierce in argument.
THALABI:v6p233/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: شدادا في الخصومة

THALABI:v6p233/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p233/r7.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v6p233/r7.claim: He glosses لدا as arguing falsely.

THALABI:v6p233/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p233/r8.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v6p233/r8.claim: He glosses لدا as contentious opponents.

THALABI:v6p233/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p233/r9.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v6p233/r9.claim: He explains the people as deaf.

THALABI:v6p233/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p233/r10.speaker: الربيع
THALABI:v6p233/r10.claim: He explains the people as having deaf hearts.

THALABI:v6p233/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p233/r11.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v6p233/r11.claim: He glosses al-aladd as an unjust person who does not act rightly.
THALABI:v6p233/r11.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الألد الظالم الذي لا يستقيم

THALABI:v6p233/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p233/r12.speaker: أبو عبيد
THALABI:v6p233/r12.claim: He defines al-aladd as one who refuses truth and claims falsehood, linking it to the Qur'anic phrase وهو ألد الخصام.
THALABI:v6p233/r12.anchor: الألد الذي لا يقبل الحق ويدعي الباطل

THALABI:v6p233/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p233/r13.speaker: عائشة
THALABI:v6p233/r13.claim: The Prophet says the most hated men to God are the bitter disputant.
THALABI:v6p233/r13.anchor: أبغض الرجال إلى الله تعالى الألد الخصم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:90-97/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:90-97/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:90-97/r10.claim: God made the Qur'an easy in the Prophet's Arabic tongue so he could give good news to the God-fearing and warn stubbornly contentious people.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p248/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p248/r4.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p248/r4.claim: Al-Suddī and others say God made the Qur'an easy in Muhammad's language; al-Hasan says people could neither recite nor understand it without this ease.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p248/r4.anchor: قوله: {فإنما يسرناه} [مريم: 97] يعني القرآن. {بلسانك} [مريم: 97] يا محمد.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The unexpressed pronoun antecedent is the Qur'an, understood from the surah's opening discussion of the prophets' shared message; omission is eloquent and signals its majesty.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the antecedent can only be the Qur’ ān.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Taysir does not mean making the Qur'an intellectually simple; it means equipping it aptly with everything needed for its purpose of instruction and reminder.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: It means making something appropriate and apt by equipping it with all that is needed for its objective.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Qawman luddan refers to the Quraysh; luddan is the plural of a term for someone belligerent and stubborn.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The latter means someone who is belligerent and stubborn.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Quraysh's tribal life and illiteracy fostered rigidity and prejudice, leading them to oppose and harass the Prophet with repeated demands.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: because of living in tribal societies and were also very rigid and prejudiced because of being unlettered.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: At the surah's close, the Qur'an is presented as apt and persuasive for conclusive communication in the Prophet's language; he must give glad tidings to the God-fearing and warn the belligerent of worldly and afterlife punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: His only obligation is to give glad tidings of success to those who fear God. As for the belligerent and aggressive among them, he should warn them of punishment in this world and in the hereafter.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p144/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p144/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p144/r1.claim: The “it” made easy is the Quran; بلسانك means in the Prophet's Arabic, with ب either meaning “upon” or linking the verb to the sense “send down.”

ALUSI-FULL:v16p144/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p144/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p144/r2.claim: The فاء connects the command to deliver the revealed surah, give its good news, and warn with it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p144/r2.anchor: والفاء لتعليل أمر ينساق اليه النضم الكريم كأنه قيل : بعد ايحاء هذه السورة الكريمة بلغ هذا المنزل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p144/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p144/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p144/r3.claim: The المتقين are either those who observe the Quran's commands and prohibitions or those drawn toward piety by it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p144/r3.anchor: المتصفين بالتقوى لامتثال ما فيه من الأمر والنهى أو الصاغرين اليها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p144/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p144/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p144/r4.claim: The stubborn opponents are likened to people who do not believe out of obstinacy and contention.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p144/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p144/r5.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v16p144/r5.claim: Raghib defines ألد as a fierce disputant who resists, relating the word to the sides of the neck.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p144/r5.anchor: واللد جمع الالد وهو كما قال الراغب : الخصم الشديد التابى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p144/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p144/r6.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p144/r6.claim: Qatada says اللد are those who argue falsely, Ibn Abbas calls them unjust, Mujahid wicked, al-Hasan deaf, and Abu Salih crooked; these describe associated traits, and the intended people are Meccans.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p144/r6.anchor: وعن قتادة اللد ذوو الجدل بالباطل الأخذون في كل لديد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p147/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p147/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p147/r7.claim: Both surahs open with disconnected letters; reports from Ibn Abbas and Jabir ibn Zayd place Taha after Maryam, whose ending about the Quran's ease and warning is reinforced by Taha's opening.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p147/r7.anchor: وينضم إلى ما ذكر اشتراك هذه السورة وسورة مريم في الأفتتاح بالحروف المقطعه

BURSEVI:v5p277#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p277#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p277#2/r1.claim: God made the Qur’an easy in the Prophet’s Arabic tongue; in context he is to convey what was revealed, offering glad tidings and warning.
BURSEVI:v5p277#2/r1.anchor: وبالفارسية (س جزاين نيست كه آسان كردانيده قرآنرا) {بلسانك} بأن أنزلناه على لفتك والباء بمعنى على

BURSEVI:v5p277#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p277#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p277#2/r2.claim: The pious are those who become God-fearing by obeying the Qur’an’s commands and prohibitions.
BURSEVI:v5p277#2/r2.anchor: أي : الصائرين إلى التقوى بامتثال ما فيه من الأمر والنهي

BURSEVI:v5p277#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p277#2/r3.speaker: القاموس
BURSEVI:v5p277#2/r3.claim: Al-Qamus explains warning someone of a matter as informing, cautioning, and frightening them about it.
BURSEVI:v5p277#2/r3.anchor: يقال انذره بالأمر إنذارا أعلمه وحذره وخوفه في إبلاغه كما في "القاموس"

BURSEVI:v5p277#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p277#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p277#2/r4.claim: Ludd is the plural of aladd: a stubborn, contentious opponent who will not turn toward truth; a hadith says such a disputant is most hated by God.
BURSEVI:v5p277#2/r4.anchor: واللد جمع الألد وهو الشديد الخصومة اللجوج المعاند

BURSEVI:v5p277#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p277#2/r5.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v5p277#2/r5.claim: A hadith describes the stubborn disputant as the person most hated by God.
BURSEVI:v5p277#2/r5.anchor: وفي الحديث "أبغض الرجال إلى الله الألد الخصم"

BURSEVI:v5p277#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p277#2/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p277#2/r6.claim: The Qur’an’s eternal divine reality cannot be contained by created, counted letters; God makes its understanding accessible to the Prophet’s heart and its recitation in clear Arabic.
BURSEVI:v5p277#2/r6.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : يشير إلى أن حقيقة القرآن التي هي صفة الله تعالى القديمة القائمة بذاته

BURSEVI:v5p277#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p277#2/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p277#2/r7.claim: The pious who receive glad tidings are three kinds: they avoid polytheism through tawhid, sins through obedience, or everything besides God through God; those warned are unbelievers fighting for falsehood, People of the Book disputing over superseded religions, and innovators or philosophers arguing falsely against truth.
BURSEVI:v5p277#2/r7.anchor: فصنف منهم يتقون الشرك بالتوحيد وصنف يتقون المعاصي بالطاعة وصنف يتقون عما سوى الله تعالى بالله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p258/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p258/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p258/r1.claim: God made the Qur'an easy in Muhammad's language so he could give good news to believers who fear God and warn combative opponents.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p258/r1.anchor: أي سهلنا القرآن بلسانك يا محمد {لتبشر به المتقين} يعني المؤمنين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p258/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p258/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p258/r2.claim: Ludd is the plural of al-ald and describes people who are severe in argument.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p258/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p258/r3.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p258/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says ludd means deaf to the truth.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p258/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p258/r4.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p258/r4.claim: Mujahid defines an ald as an unjust person who does not act rightly.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p258/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p258/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p258/r5.claim: Abu ʿUbayda says an ald refuses truth and asserts falsehood.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p258/r5.anchor: أبو عبيدة: "الألد" الذي لا يقبل الحق ويدعي الباطل.

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:97-98/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:97-98/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:97-98/r1.claim: God made the Quran easy in Muhammad’s language; the bāʾ can mean “in” or retain its ordinary sense because the verb implies sending down. The warning addresses contentious people who pursue every line of dispute.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:97-98/r1.anchor: والباء بمعنى على أو على أصله

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:97-98/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:97-98/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:97-98/r3.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet promises ten good deeds to whoever recites Maryam for each person who disbelieved in or affirmed the named prophets and each person who prayed or did not pray to God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:97-98/r3.anchor: من قرأ سورة مريم أعطي عشر حسنات بعدد من كذب زكريا

DURR-FULL:v5p546/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p546/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p546/r1.claim: Qatada identifies the “stubborn people” warned by the Qur’an as Quraysh.
DURR-FULL:v5p546/r1.anchor: عن قتادة {قوما لدا} قال: هم قريش

DURR-FULL:v5p546/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p546/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p546/r2.claim: Mujahid explains ludd as people who do not act uprightly.

QUSHAYRI:v2p247/r31.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p247/r31.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p247/r31.claim: The same speech and address brings ease to some and warning to others; felicity belongs to those enabled to receive the facilitation, while the forsaken face woe despite the warning.
QUSHAYRI:v2p247/r31.anchor: الكلام واحد والخطاب واحد ، وهو لقوم تيسير ، ولآخرين تخويف وتحذير فطوبى لمن يسر لما وفق به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p175/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p175/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p175/r1.claim: The verse signals the sūra’s close: after varied narratives, lessons, promises, and warnings, a comprehensive ending praises the Quran and explains purposes of its revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p175/r1.anchor: إيذان بانتهاء السورة ، فإن شأن الإتيان بكلام جامع بعد أفنان الحديث أن يؤذن بأن المتكلم سيطوي بساطه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p175/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p175/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p175/r2.claim: The fa may be explicative, implying that the Prophet must convey the revelation despite the polytheists’ anger at its refutation and warnings; they had offered to follow if he stopped condemning their gods and ancestors.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p175/r2.anchor: فيجوز جعل الفاء فصيحة مؤذنة بكلام مقدر يدل عليه المذكور ، كأنه قيل : بلغ ما أنزلنا إليك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p175/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p175/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p175/r3.claim: Alternatively, the fa branches from the judgment and promise in 19:94–96: the Quran was made easy for the Prophet so he can warn the obstinate and give glad tidings to believers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p175/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الفاء للتفريع على وعيد الكافرين بقوله : { لقد أحصاهم وعدم عدا وكلهم آتيه يوم القيامة فردا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p175/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p175/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p175/r4.claim: The pronoun refers to the Quran; making it easy means facilitating its recitation, as in 54:32.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p175/r4.anchor: وضمير الغائب عائد إلى القرآن بدلالة السياق مثل : { حتى توارت بالحجاب } ( ص : 32 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p175/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p175/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p175/r5.claim: Lisānik means the Prophet’s language, Arabic; its excellence, eloquence, and ease of recitation contribute to the Quran’s distinction and memorability compared with earlier scriptures.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p175/r5.anchor: واللسان : اللغة ، أي بلغتك ، وهي العربية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p176/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p176/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p176/r1.claim: The bāʾ means either cause or accompaniment.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p176/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p176/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p176/r2.claim: Ludd condemns them as deeply adversarial and resistant to admitting truth; it is the plural of aladd, and shirk led Arabs to mix this vice with otherwise praiseworthy traits.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p176/r2.anchor: وعبر عن الكفار بقوم لد ذما لهم بأنهم أهل إيغال في المراء والمكابرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p176/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p176/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p176/r3.claim: A sound Prophetic report calls the intensely disputatious adversary the person most hated by God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p176/r3.anchor: وفي الحديث الصحيح : ( أبغض الرجال إلى الله الألد الخصم )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p176/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p176/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p176/r4.claim: Pairing the God-fearing with the obstinate contrasts obedience with rebellion; it also implies their disbelief comes from deliberate stubbornness despite knowing Muhammad’s truth, as 6:33 says.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p176/r4.anchor: وقد حسن مقابلة المتقين بقوم لد ، لأن التقوى امتثال وطاعة والشرك عصيان ولدد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p176/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p176/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p176/r5.claim: Calling them a “people” marks obstinacy as their defining collective trait, as in descriptions of people who reason or do not believe at 2:164 and 10:101.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p176/r5.anchor: وإيقاع لفظ القوم عليهم للإشارة إلى أن اللدد شأنهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r1.claim: The pronoun in “We made it easy” refers to the Quran, although it was not just named, as in the verse about the sun disappearing behind a veil.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r1.anchor: الضمير في «يسرنا» للقرآن، وهذا كقوله حتى توارت بالحجاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r2.claim: The Quran is made easy in Muhammad's clear, understandable language.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r2.anchor: ووقع التيسير في كونه بلسان محمد عليه السرم وبلغته المفهومة المبينة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r3.claim: Glad tidings for the God-fearing are Paradise, lasting bliss, and honor in this world.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r3.anchor: وبشارة المتقين هي الجنة والنعيم الدائم والعز في الدنيا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r4.claim: The contentious people are Quraysh, disputing falsely; al-aladd is extreme in argument.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r4.anchor: و «القوم اللد» هم قريش ومعناه مجادلين مخاصمين بباطل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r5.speaker: مجاهِد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r5.claim: Mujāhid glosses ludd as wicked; the author specifies wicked contention and says true aladd contention is false.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r6.speaker: رسول الله
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r6.claim: A hadith says the most hateful men to God are fiercely contentious litigants.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r6.anchor: وفي الحديث «أبغض الرجال إلى الله تعالى الألد الخصم»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r7.claim: Because scripture condemns their contentiousness, God answers their pride with warnings about destroying people more powerful and argumentative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r7.anchor: وجب أن يفسد عليهم بالوعيد والتمثيل بإهلاك من كان أشد منهم وألد وأعظم قدرا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r8.claim: Arabs in ignorance and unbelief boasted of contentiousness as intelligence and manliness; a poem illustrates the pride.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r8.anchor: فإن العرب لجهالتها وعتوها وكفرها كانت تتمدح باللد وتراه إدراكا وشهامة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r9.claim: Other commentators gloss ludd as evildoers or wrongdoers; the author summarizes the sense as contentiousness.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34#3/r9.anchor: وعبر المفسرون عن «اللد» بالفجرة وبالظلمة وتلخيص معناها ما ذكرناه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p267/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p267/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p267/r1.claim: Ibn Qutayba says the Quran was made easy and revealed in the Prophet's language.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p267/r1.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة أي سهلناه وأنزلناه بلغتك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p267/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p267/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p267/r2.claim: Ludd is the plural of aladd, meaning a disputatious opponent.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p267/r2.anchor: واللد جمع ألد وهو الخصم الجدل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p269/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p269/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p269/r1.claim: The report that this verse was revealed during ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf's migration is erroneous: the whole sura is Meccan, none was revealed after Hijra, and the chain is unsound.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p269/r1.anchor: وقد روى ابن جرير أثرا أن هذه الآية نزلت في هجرة عبد الرحمن بن عوف. وهو خطأ، فإن هذه السورة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p269/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p269/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p269/r2.claim: God made the Qur'an easy in Muhammad's clear, eloquent Arabic so he may give glad tidings to responsive believers and warn stubborn resisters of truth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p269/r2.anchor: وقوله: {فإنما يسرناه} يعني: القرآن، {بلسانك} أي: يا محمد، وهو اللسان العربي المبين الفصيح الكامل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p269/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p269/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p269/r3.claim: Mujahid glosses ludd as people who do not become upright.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p269/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p269/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p269/r4.claim: Al-Suddi explains the ludd as crooked and turned from truth; other reports call them contentious, lying, deaf-hearted, Quraysh, wicked, or oppressive.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p269/r4.anchor: عن إسماعيل -وهو السدي-عن أبي صالح: {وتنذر به قوما لدا} عوجا عن الحق.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p269/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p269/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p269/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says ludd means oppressive and cites the description “most contentious in argument.”
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p269/r5.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: الألد: الظلوم، وقرأ قول الله: {وهو ألد الخصام} [البقرة: 204] .

JISHUMI:v6p4621/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4621/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4621/r8.claim: Ladd means intense disputation; the Qurʾānic phrase aladd al-khiṣām denotes the most contentious dispute, and aladd has the plural aludd.
JISHUMI:v6p4621/r8.anchor: اللدد: شدة الخصومة، وفي التنزيل: (ألد الخصام) أي: أشد الخصام خصومة

JISHUMI:v6p4621/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4621/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4621/r13.claim: Ludd is an adjective modifying qawman.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p49/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p49/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p49/r1.claim: This is the sura's conclusion: relay the revelation, which God made easy and clear in the Prophet's eloquent Arabic, to give good news and warning.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p49/r1.anchor: خاتمة السورة ومقطعها ، فكأنه قال : بلغ هذا المنزل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p49/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p49/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p49/r2.claim: Ludd are fierce disputants in falsehood, taking every side of argument through obstinacy; the intended people are Meccans.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p49/r2.anchor: الشداد الخصومة بالباطل ، الآخذون في كل لديد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p49/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p49/r6.speaker: رسول الله
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p49/r6.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet promises ten good deeds for each named prophet and believer who denied or affirmed them, and for those who supplicate or do not supplicate, to whoever recites Sūrat Maryam.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p49/r6.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 682 ) ( من قرأ سورة مريم

MUJAHID:v1p391#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p391#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p391#3/r1.claim: Mujahid says the stubborn people described as luddan do not straighten themselves or become upright.
MUJAHID:v1p391#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ وتنذر به قوما لدا ﴾ يقول لا يستقيمون

NASAFI-FULL:v3p49#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p49#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p49#5/r1.claim: God has made the Qur'an easy in the Prophet's language, as a circumstantial phrase, to give good news to believers who are pious.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p49#5/r1.anchor: سهلنا القرآن ﴿ بلسانك ﴾ لغتك حال ﴿ لتبشر به المتقين ﴾ المؤمنين

NASAFI-FULL:v3p49#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p49#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p49#5/r2.claim: لدا means fierce in false disputation: they take every side of argument; the plural is ألد, and the intended people are Meccans.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p49#5/r2.anchor: شدادا في الخصومة بالباطل أي الذين يأخذون في كل لديد أي شق من المراء والجدال جمع ألد يريد به أهل مكة

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p276#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p276#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p276#4/r1.claim: Yassarnāhu means We made it easy and revealed it in your language.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p276#4/r1.anchor: {فإنما يسرناه بلسانك} أي سهلناه وأنزلناه بلغتك.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p276#4/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p276#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p276#4/r2.claim: Ludd is the plural of aladd, a contentious disputant.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p276#4/r2.anchor: و (اللد) جمع ألد. وهو الخصم الجدل.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p276#4/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p276#4/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p276#4/r3.claim: Al-rakz is a sound that cannot be understood.

MAJAZ:v2p12/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p12/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p12/r4.claim: لدا means contentious disputants; its singular ألد describes someone who refuses truth and argues for falsehood. Muhalhil’s ألد ذا مغلاق and Ruʾba’s الألواد/الألداد attest the forms.
MAJAZ:v2p12/r4.anchor: «قوما لدا» (97) واحدهم: ألد، وهو الشديد الخصومة الذي لا يقبل الحق ويدعى الباطل

MAJAZ:v2p12/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p12/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p12/r5.claim: A reported variant for Muhalhil’s line is مغلاق الحجة.
MAJAZ:v2p12/r5.anchor: ويروى مغلاق الحجة عن أبى عبيدة

QURTUBI-FULL:19:97/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:97/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:97/r1.claim: God clarified the Qurʾān in the Prophet’s Arabic tongue and made it easy for those who reflect; alternatively, it was revealed in Arabic so its audience could readily understand it.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:97/r1.anchor: يعني بيناه بلسانك العربي وجعلناه سهلا على من تدبره وتأمله

QURTUBI-FULL:19:97/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:97/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:97/r2.claim: The glad tidings are for believers; “ludd” is the plural of “aladd,” fiercely disputatious, as in 2:204, and a cited poem illustrates it.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:97/r2.anchor: اللُد جمع الألد وهو الشديد الخصومة

QURTUBI-FULL:19:97/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:97/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:19:97/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayda defines the disputatious person as one who rejects truth and asserts falsehood.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:97/r3.anchor: الألد الذي لا يقبل الحق ويدعي الباطل

QURTUBI-FULL:19:97/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:97/r4.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:19:97/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan says “ludd” are people deaf to truth.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:97/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:97/r5.speaker: الربيع
QURTUBI-FULL:19:97/r5.claim: Al-Rabīʿ describes them as the ears of the heart being deaf.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:97/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:97/r6.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:19:97/r6.claim: Mujāhid glosses the group as wicked people.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:97/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:97/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:19:97/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās calls them fierce in argument.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:97/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:97/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:97/r9.claim: Another explanation is unjust people who refuse to act rightly; the meanings are close and this group is singled out because less stubborn people are easier to guide.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:97/r9.anchor: وقيل: الظالم الذي لا يستقيم والمعنى واحد

STUDYQURAN:19:97/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:97/r1.speaker: IK, R, Z
STUDYQURAN:19:97/r1.claim: God made the Quran easy on the Prophet's tongue by revealing it in Arabic, the native language of the Prophet and his Companions.
STUDYQURAN:19:97/r1.anchor: by revealing it in Arabic (IK, R, Z), the native language of the Prophet and his Companions.

STUDYQURAN:19:97/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:97/r2.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:19:97/r2.claim: An alternate reading takes the phrase as making the Quran easy in the Prophet's language, referring to its revelation in Arabic.
STUDYQURAN:19:97/r2.anchor: easy in thy tongue [i.e., in the Prophet’s language],” referring to the revelation of the Quran in Arabic (Z)

STUDYQURAN:19:97/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:97/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:97/r3.claim: Other verses say the Quran was made easy to remember.
STUDYQURAN:19:97/r3.anchor: See also 54:17, 22, 32, and 40, where the Quran is said to have been made easy to remember.

STUDYQURAN:19:97/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:97/r4.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:19:97/r4.claim: Luddan are intensely but vainly argumentative people who argue from falsehood.
STUDYQURAN:19:97/r4.anchor: Contentious translates luddan, which denotes those who are intensely but vainly argumentative and who argue on the basis of falsehood (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:19:97/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:97/r5.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:19:97/r5.claim: The term also suggests insolence and deafness to hearing the truth.
STUDYQURAN:19:97/r5.anchor: also connotes an attitude of insolence and a certain “deafness” to hearing the truth (Ṭ)

TAB-FULL:v15p645/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p645/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p645/r1.claim: The Qur'an is made easy for Muhammad to recite in his tongue to announce Paradise to the God-fearing; he must also warn Quraysh, who refuse truth through stubborn false disputation.
TAB-FULL:v15p645/r1.anchor: قريش، فإنهم أهل لدد وجدل بالباطل، لا يقبلون الحق

TAB-FULL:v15p645/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p645/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p645/r2.claim: Al-Tabari defines ludd as intense contentiousness and says these people reject the truth.
TAB-FULL:v15p645/r2.anchor: لا يقبلون الحق. واللد: شدة الخصومة

TAB-FULL:v15p645/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p645/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p645/r3.claim: Mujahid says the ludd do not remain upright.
TAB-FULL:v15p645/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {لدا} [مريم: 97] قال: لا يستقيمون

TAB-FULL:v15p645/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p645/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p645/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the ludd as unjust people.
TAB-FULL:v15p645/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله {وتنذر به قوما لدا} [مريم: 97] يقول: لتنذر به قوما ظلمة

TAB-FULL:v15p645/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p645/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p645/r5.claim: Qatada describes them as people who argue falsely and are stubborn and contentious.
TAB-FULL:v15p645/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، {وتنذر به قوما لدا} [مريم: 97] أي جدالا بالباطل، ذوي لدد وخصومة

TAB-FULL:v15p645/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p645/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p645/r6.claim: Mujahid also glosses them as wicked people.
TAB-FULL:v15p645/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {وتنذر به قوما لدا} [مريم: 97] قال: فجارا

TAB-FULL:v15p645/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p645/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v15p645/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says al-aladd means oppressive and cites 2:204, where God calls an adversary intensely contentious.
TAB-FULL:v15p645/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {وتنذر به قوما لدا} [مريم: 97] قال: الألد: الظلوم، وقرأ قول الله: {وهو ألد الخصام} [البقرة: 204]

TAB-FULL:v15p645/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p645/r8.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v15p645/r8.claim: Al-Hasan says they are deaf to the truth.
TAB-FULL:v15p645/r8.anchor: عن الحسن، في قول الله عز وجل: {وتنذر به قوما لدا} [مريم: 97] قال: صما عن الحق

TAB-FULL:v15p645/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p645/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p645/r9.claim: Al-Tabari does not restate the term's earlier explanation because he has already explained al-aladd with supporting evidence.
TAB-FULL:v15p645/r9.anchor: وقد بينا معنى الألد فيما مضى بشواهده، فأغنى ذلك عن إعادته في هذا الموضع

TABATABAI:19:97-98/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:97-98/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:97-98/r1.claim: The surah closes by describing the Quran’s descent from its inaccessible reality into the Prophet’s speech, so he can give glad tidings to the pious, warn stubborn opponents, and recall earlier peoples’ destruction.
TABATABAI:19:97-98/r1.anchor: الآيتان ختام السورة يذكر سبحانه فيهما تنزيل حقيقة القرآن وهي أعلى من أن تنالها أيدى الأفهام العادية

TABATABAI:19:97-98/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:97-98/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:97-98/r2.claim: Facilitation implies an earlier state in which the Quran was not readily recited or understood; al-Zukhruf describes it as lofty and resistant to ordinary understanding before it was made Arabic.
TABATABAI:19:97-98/r2.anchor: التيسير وهو التسهيل ينبئ عن حال سابقة ما كان يسهل معها تلاوته ولا فهمه

TABATABAI:19:97-98/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:97-98/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:97-98/r3.claim: The preferred sense of making it easy in the Prophet’s tongue is rendering it in Arabic, which makes warning and glad tidings possible and better fits the earlier verses and surah context.
TABATABAI:19:97-98/r3.anchor: فتنبئ الآية أنه تعالى يسره بلسانه ليتيسر له التبشير والإنذار

TABATABAI:19:97-98/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:97-98/r4.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:19:97-98/r4.claim: An alternative says God made the Quran flow on the Prophet’s tongue through revelation and singled him out to receive divine speech; the author considers it profound but less fitting to context.
TABATABAI:19:97-98/r4.anchor: وربما قيل إن معنى تيسيره بلسانه إجراؤه على لسانه بالوحي واختصاصه بوحي الكلام الإلهي

TABATABAI:19:97-98/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:97-98/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:97-98/r5.claim: The ludd are the Prophet’s people, and the word is the plural of aladd, meaning a fierce disputant.
TABATABAI:19:97-98/r5.anchor: المراد قومه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم، واللد جمع ألد من اللدد وهو الخصومة

TABRISI:19:97-98/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:97-98/r10.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:19:97-98/r10.claim: Abū Muslim says God made the Qurʾān easy by revealing it in the Prophet’s Arabic language so its hearers could understand it.
TABRISI:19:97-98/r10.anchor: يسرنا القرآن بأن أنزلناه بلسانك وهي لغة العرب ليسهل عليهم معرفته

TABRISI:19:97-98/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:97-98/r11.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:19:97-98/r11.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī alternatively says God made Qurʾānic recitation easy for the Prophet and enabled him to recite it.
TABRISI:19:97-98/r11.anchor: وقيل: معناه يسرناه قراءة القرآن على لسانك ومكناك من قراءته عن الجبائي

TABRISI:19:97-98/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:97-98/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:97-98/r12.claim: The glad tidings are for those who avoid associating partners with God and major sins, informing them of what pleases them among God’s promises.
TABRISI:19:97-98/r12.anchor: الذين يتقون الشرك والكبائر أي تخبرهم بما تسرهم مما أعده الله لهم

TABRISI:19:97-98/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:97-98/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:19:97-98/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says ludd means fierce in dispute and identifies the people as Quraysh.
TABRISI:19:97-98/r13.anchor: شدادا في الخصومة عن ابن عباس يعني قريشا

TABRISI:19:97-98/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:97-98/r14.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:19:97-98/r14.claim: Qatāda interprets ludd as people given to argument and disputation.
TABRISI:19:97-98/r14.anchor: قوما ذوي جدل مخاصمين عن قتادة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r1.claim: God made the Qurʾān easy and revealed it in the Prophet’s language to ease his delivery of the message.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {فإنما يسرناه بلسانك} أي: هوناه وأنزلناه بلغتك ليسهل عليك الإبلاغ

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r2.claim: The Qurʾān gives glad tidings to those who obey the Prophet and warns those who disobey him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r2.anchor: {لتبشر به} أي: بالقرآن من أطاعك {وتنذر} من عصاك.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r3.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r3.claim: Al-Kalbī glosses it as making the Qurʾān easy upon the Prophet’s tongue; on this reading, lisān does not mean language.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r3.anchor: وقال الكلبي: (هوناه على لسانك) (¬2). وعلى هذا لم يرد باللسان اللغة.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r4.speaker: أبو صالح
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r4.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ glosses ludd as people turned away from the truth.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r5.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r5.claim: Mujāhid glosses ludd as people who do not act uprightly.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r6.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r6.claim: Qatāda glosses ludd as people who argue falsely.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r7.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r7.anchor: وروي عن الحسن أنه قال في "تفسيره": (صما) (¬7).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r8.speaker: الربيع
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r8.claim: Al-Rabīʿ clarifies the ‘deaf’ gloss as deafness of the hearts’ ears.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r8.anchor: وزاد الربيع بيانا فقال: (صم آذان القلوب) (¬8).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r9.claim: The author says the other glosses express aspects of ludd, while Qatāda gives its tafsīr: false argument stems from deaf hearts that fail to understand the Prophet’s message.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r9.anchor: وهذه الأقوال كلها معنى وليس بتفسير. والتفسير قول قتادة، وذلك أن خصومتهم بالباطل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r10.claim: The author points back to his discussion of al-idd in Q. 2:204.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r10.anchor: وذكرنا الكلام في هذا الحرف عند قوله: {ألد الخصام} [البقرة: 204].

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r11.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r11.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says the obstinate disputants are singled out for warning because others will follow once proof is established, while the uncontentious submit quickly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p341/r11.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: (وخص اللد بالإنذار؛ لأنهم إذا قامت عليه الحجة صار غيرهم لاحقا بهم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p249/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p249/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p249/r1.claim: The good tidings are conveyed through the Qur'an.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p249/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p249/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p249/r2.claim: The people given good tidings are the God-fearing, who are promised Paradise.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p249/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p249/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p249/r3.claim: The warning of the fire is conveyed through the Qur'an.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p249/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p249/r4.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p249/r4.claim: Qatāda glosses the stubborn people as disputants in falsehood and people prone to contentious argument.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p249/r4.anchor: سعيد عن قتادة قال: أي جدلاء بالباطل وذوي لدد وخصومة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p249/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p249/r5.speaker: يحيى
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p249/r5.claim: Yaḥyā identifies the contentious people as Quraysh, citing 43:57-58, which calls them disputatious.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p249/r5.anchor: قال يحيى: يعني قريشا وكقوله: {إذا قومك منه يصدون} [الزخرف: 57] إلى قوله: {بل هم قوم خصمون} [الزخرف: 58]

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p249/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p249/r6.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p249/r6.claim: Mujāhid says the stubborn people do not stand upright.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:97/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:97/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:97/r1.claim: God sent each prophet's message in the language of his people; the Arabic Qur'an was made understandable to the Arab Prophet so he could understand and clearly convey its good news and warnings.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:97/r1.anchor: Kur’an’ı da Arap olan Hz. Peygamber’e Arapça olarak indirmek ve anlaşılır kılmak suretiyle kolaylaştırmıştır

SAMIN-DURR:19:97/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:97/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:97/r1.claim: بلسانك may modify an omitted participle as a circumstantial phrase: the Quran was made or sent down in your language, where لسان means language.
SAMIN-DURR:19:97/r1.anchor: قوله: { بلسانك }: يجوز أن يكون متعلقا بمحذوف على أنه حال.

SAMIN-DURR:19:97/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:97/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:97/r2.claim: A reported analysis takes بلسانك to mean على, but the author says that is unnecessary and has no clear sense.
SAMIN-DURR:19:97/r2.anchor: وقيل: هي بمعنى على، وهذا لا حاجة إليه بل لا يظهر له معنى.

SAMIN-DURR:19:97/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:97/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:97/r3.claim: لدا is the plural of ألد, one intensely contentious, like حمر as plural of أحمر.
SAMIN-DURR:19:97/r3.anchor: و " لدا " جمع ألد " وهو الشديد الخصومة كالحمر جمع أحمر.

ZAJJAJ:v3p346/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p346/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p346/r7.claim: لدا is the plural of ألد, like صم from أصم, and means people fiercely given to dispute.
ZAJJAJ:v3p346/r7.anchor: جمع ألد مثل أصم وصم، والألد الشديد الخصومة

ASAD-NOTES:19:96#n81/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:96#n81/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:19:96#n81/r1.claim: Because people cannot comprehend God's word directly, revelation comes in human language and accessible concepts, described as brought down upon or alighting on the Prophet's heart.
ASAD-NOTES:19:96#n81/r1.anchor: it has always been revealed to him in his own, human tongue (cf. 14:4

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Qur’an is the Prophet’s means to warn and give glad tidings; those receptive will believe, refusers will face their fate, and he need not worry about them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The Prophet (sws) is told that the Qur’ān is the best instrument to warn people and give them glad tidings.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Only believers will succeed on the Day of Judgment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Only the believers will succeed on the Day of Judgement.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The preceding analysis makes the sūrah’s structure and coherence evident.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the structure and coherence of the sūrah becomes very evident.

QIRAAT-ER:19:97:7#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:19:97:7#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:19:97:7#1/r1.claim: Form I tabshura removes doubled shin from Form II tubashshira, shifting from solemn heralding to plain informing.
QIRAAT-ER:19:97:7#1/r1.anchor: Form I (tabshura) vs. Form II (tubashshira) — removes doubled shin; simpler announcement

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p13#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p13#2/r2.speaker: عائشة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p13#2/r2.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet most disliked the combative, disputatious man.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p13#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج عن ابن أبي مليكة عن عائشة قالت كان أبغض الرجال إلى رسول الله الألد الخصم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p14/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p14/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p14/r1.claim: Qatada glosses luddan as arguing falsely.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p14/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ لدا ﴾ قال جدلا بالباطل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r10.claim: The pronoun in يسرناه refers to the Qur'an: God made it easy in the Prophet's language, meaning clear Arabic.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r10.anchor: والضمير في يسرناه عائد على القرآن، أي أنزلناه عليك ميسرا سهلا بلسانك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r11.claim: Glad tidings tell the pious what will please them, including their reward for piety.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r11.anchor: لتبشر به المتقين أي تخبرهم بما يسرهم وبما يكون لهم من الثواب على تقواهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses لدا as unjust people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r12.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: لدا ظلمة، ومجاهد فجارا، والحسن صما،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r13.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r13.claim: Mujahid glosses لدا as wicked people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r13.anchor: ومجاهد فجارا، والحسن صما، وأبو صالح عوجا عن الحق،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r14.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r14.claim: Hasan glosses لدا as deaf people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r14.anchor: والحسن صما، وأبو صالح عوجا عن الحق،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r15.speaker: أبو صالح
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r15.claim: Abu Salih glosses لدا as people who turn away from truth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r15.anchor: وأبو صالح عوجا عن الحق، وقتادة ذوي جدل بالباطل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r16.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r16.claim: Qatada glosses لدا as people who argue falsely and stubbornly take every side in dispute; the intended audience is Meccans.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r16.anchor: وقتادة ذوي جدل بالباطل آخذين في كل لديد بالمراء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r17.claim: The warning about many destroyed before them threatens the obstinate people; قبلهم refers to قوما لدا.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r17.anchor: وكم أهلكنا تخويف لهم وإنذار بالإهلاك بالعذاب والضمير في قوله قبلهم عائد على قوما لدا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r18.claim: هل تحس is an interrogative whose force is negation: you perceive none of them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r18.anchor: وهل تحس استفهام معناه النفي أي لا تحس.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r19.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r19.claim: The majority read هل تحس as the present tense of أحس.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r19.anchor:
وقرأ الجمهور:
هل تحس مضارع أحس.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r20.speaker: أبو حيوة، أبو بحرية، ابن أبي عبلة، أبو جعفر المدني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r20.claim: These readers use تحس with an open tā and ḍamma on ḥā.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r20.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وأبو بحرية وابن أبي عبلة وأبو جعفر المدني تحس بفتح التاء وضم الحاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r21.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r21.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r21.claim: Another reading derives تحس from حسّ, to sense or perceive, the root of words for senses and perceptible things.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r21.anchor: وقرىء تحس من حسه إذا شعر به ومنه الحواس والمحسوسات.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r22.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r22.speaker: حنظلة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r22.claim: Hanzala reads أو تسمع as a passive verb, something heard.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r22.anchor: وقرأ حنظلة أو تسمع مضارع أسمعت مبنيا للمفعول.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r23.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r23.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r23.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses الركز as a faint, quiet sound.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r23.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الركز الصوت الخفي.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r24.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r24.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r24.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses الركز as sound or perception.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r25.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r25.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r25.claim: Hasan says that when the punishment came, no person remained to see and no sound could be heard.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r25.anchor: وقال الحسن: لما أتاهم عذابنا لم يبق منهم شخص يرى ولا صوت يسمع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r26.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r26.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r26.claim: Another explanation is that they died and were forgotten, so no one reports anything about them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p305/r26.anchor: وقيل: المعنى ماتوا ونسي ذكرهم فلا يخبر عنهم مخبر.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p167/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p167/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p167/r1.claim: In roughly contemporaneous, nearby suras, the Qur'an argues for Muhammad's prophethood through stories of earlier messengers whom their peoples also denied and challenged.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p167/r1.anchor: وفي هذه السور التي تقارب وقت نزولها، كما تقارب ترتيبها في المصحف، يبدو التركيز، في الاحتجاج للمعجزة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p167/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p167/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p167/r2.claim: The Qur'an is a clear Arabic book revealed from the Lord of the worlds and made easy in the Prophet's language to give glad tidings and warnings.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p167/r2.anchor: كتاب عربي مبين، تنزيل من رب العالمين، نزل به الوحي على خاتم المرسلين، ويسره بلسانه ليبشر به المتقين وينذر به قوماً لداً

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p167/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p167/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p167/r4.claim: The author notes the changing lengths of the disconnected-letter openings, from single letters through five, and says Arabic words are built from the same letters as the clear Arabic Book.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p167/r4.anchor: ألفاظ العربية مبنية على مثل هذا العدد من الأحرف التي نزل بها الكتاب العربي المبين

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p167/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p167/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p167/r5.claim: The disconnected letters may look like meaningless foreign strings, but their secret becomes clear when each letter takes its place in eloquent expression.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p167/r5.anchor: أن الحروف قد تتألف منها ألفاظ عجماء، فإذا أخذ الحرف موضعه في البيان، تجلى سره

BURHAN:v1p98/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p98/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p98/r5.claim: The verse counters listed here were not counted as endings because they did not match their neighboring endings, including لِتُبَشِّرَ بِهِ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ in Maryam.
BURHAN:v1p98/r5.anchor: ومن ثم أجمع العادون على ترك عد ﴿ ويأت بآخرين ﴾ و ﴿ ولا الملائكة المقربون ﴾

KHATTABI:v1p21#2/r1.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p21#2/r1.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p21#2/r1.claim: Scholars have proposed many explanations of the Qur'an's inimitability without settling its precise mechanism, but the continuing fact of human inability is unmistakable.
KHATTABI:v1p21#2/r1.anchor: لتعذر معرفة وجه الإعجاز في القرآن

KHATTABI:v1p21#2/r2.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p21#2/r2.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p21#2/r2.claim: Muhammad challenged all the Arabs to produce a sura and kept demanding it for twenty years while denouncing their beliefs and judgment; they instead fought him, losing lives, kinship, and property.
KHATTABI:v1p21#2/r2.anchor: وقد بقى صلى الله عليه وسلم يطالبهم به مدة عشرين سنة

KHATTABI:v1p21#2/r3.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p21#2/r3.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p21#2/r3.claim: If they had the ability, they would have chosen the easy verbal challenge over costly war; as with a thirsty person who dies beside drinkable water, failure to answer proves incapacity.
KHATTABI:v1p21#2/r3.anchor: لو كان ذلك في وسعهم وتحت أقدارهم لم يتكلفوا هذه الأمور الخطيرة

KHATTABI:v1p21#2/r4.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p21#2/r4.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p21#2/r4.claim: Quraysh had intelligent minds, skilled orators, and accomplished poets; the Qur'an also calls them contentious and ludd, so their failure to exploit the challenge is evidence of inability.
KHATTABI:v1p21#2/r4.anchor: فقال سبحانه: {ما ضربوه لك إلا جدلا بل هم قوم خصمون}

DAMGHANI:v1p502/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p502/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p502/r9.claim: Yusr and taysīr mean facilitation or making something easy, including the Qur'an and God's provision of an easy outcome.
DAMGHANI:v1p502/r9.anchor: الخامس اليسر والتيسير التسهيل قوله تعالى في سورة مريم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p159/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p159/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p159/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir's observation also fits Maryam: five repetitions of 'remember in the Book' and the surah's closing reference to the Qur'an refute Rida's exception.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p159/r3.anchor: يطرد ملحظ ابن كثير، لا تتخلف عنه سورة مريم - كما وهم السيد رضا - وفيها يتكرر قوله تعالى للمصطفى
